content:
Container image Images are published to the GitHub Container Registry:
podman pull ghcr.io/contre95/stella:beta # newest releaseEvery version is listed in GitHub packages. There is deliberately no latest tag: pin a version, or track beta.
Tag What it is vX.Y.Z An exact release, immutable beta Newest release, the tag to follow nightly main as of 02:00 UTC Running The web UI listens on port 8858; the MCP endpoint, when enabled, is served on the same port at /mcp. The image ships config.example.yaml as /app/config.yaml, and keeps its database and uploaded media under /app/data.
podman run -d \ --name stella \ -p 8858:8858 \ -v /host/stella/data:/app/data \ -v /host/stella/config.yaml:/app/config.yaml \ ghcr.io/contre95/stella:betaThe config path can be changed with STELLA_CONFIG_PATH. See Configuration for every setting.
Building it yourself IMAGE_TAG=stella podman build -t stella .IMAGE_TAG is baked in as an env var and is what the UI shows as its version; it falls back to dev when unset.
Running from source With devenv + Nix:
devenv up # Go + Tailwind CLI provided, CSS rebuilt on shell entry, runs the serverOtherwise:
go run ./srcpublic/css/app.css is generated by Tailwind from styles/input.css. A compiled copy is committed so go run works out of the box; rebuild it if you change styles or template class names (devenv does it for you).

title: Self hosted

content:
Stella reads config.yaml from the working directory, or from the path in STELLA_CONFIG_PATH. This is the full example config (config.example.yaml in the repo), with every setting at its default:
dbPath: ./data/stella.db # Directory where uploaded card images are stored. imagePath: ./data/images # IANA timezone (e.g. Europe/Madrid) used for review-day boundaries and sent # to sync devices so their clocks show local time, DST included. # Empty = the host's local timezone. timezone: "" server: port: 8858 appName: Stella bodyLimit: 10485760 auth: enabled: false publicURLs: [] oidc: issuer: "" clientID: "" clientSecret: "" cimd: false mcp: # Enable the MCP endpoint at /mcp (StreamableHTTP transport). enabled: false refreshTokenDays: 30 logger: level: info # debug | info | warn | error format: "" # logfmt (default) | text | json review: # Hour (0-23) at which a new study day begins. dayStartsAt: 3 # How many not-yet-retained cards to juggle at once. nonMemorisedCardsInHand: 10 # Cap on the scheduled interval in days; 0 = no cap. maxScheduledIntervalDays: 0 # Shuffle due cards instead of ordering by interval. randomiseScheduledCards: false # Shuffle the order unseen cards are introduced. randomiseNewCards: false cards: # Automatically play audio when a card (front or back) is shown. autoplayAudio: trueauth is explained in Users & login. mcp is explained in MCP server. review tunes the scheduler, see Reviewing. server.bodyLimit is the largest request body in bytes (10 MiB by default), which caps the size of uploaded media and imported archives.
summary: Stella reads config.yaml from the working directory, or from the path in STELLA_CONFIG_PATH. This is the full example config (config.example.yaml in the repo), with every setting at its default:
title: Configuration

content:
Stella runs in one of two modes, controlled by auth.enabled.
Single user auth.enabled: false (the default). There is no login, and all data belongs to one built-in local account. The /mcp endpoint (when enabled) has no auth either, so put it behind a trusted network (Tailscale, localhost, VPN) if you expose it.
This is meant for the lone self-hoster who is the only user of their services.
Multi user auth.enabled: true. Login goes through any OpenID Connect provider (Keycloak, Authentik, Pocket ID, …) configured under auth.oidc, and each user gets their own decks, cards and review history. This mode is for self-hosters who want to share Stella with friends and family.
auth: enabled: true publicURLs: - https://stella.example.com - http://192.168.1.50:8858 oidc: issuer: https://id.example.com clientID: stella clientSecret: ...publicURLs lists the external base URLs Stella is reachable at: usually one, but list more (a LAN address and a public domain, say) if you reach it several ways. Requests are matched to one of them by Host header, falling back to the first. Register <publicURL>/auth/callback as a redirect URI at the provider for each one. oidc.issuer is the provider’s issuer URL; its discovery document must live at <issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration. oidc.cimd: true makes Stella register itself through a self-hosted Client ID Metadata Document (<publicURL>/auth/client-metadata.json) instead of clientID/clientSecret: no client record to create, just allowlist that URL at the provider for each public URL. Only providers implementing CIMD (such as Pocket ID) support it, and it can’t be combined with clientID/clientSecret. Tokens /settings/tokens creates bearer tokens for MCP clients and sync devices, and lists the OAuth apps connected to your account so you can revoke them. A token is shown only once, when it is created.
summary:

content:
Data model Group: an optional folder for decks. A deck belongs to at most one group. Deck: a named collection of facts (name up to 32 characters, description, optional cover image, optional group). Tag: a free label; a deck can carry any number of them, independent of groups. Fact: the content itself, a front and a back, plus an optional image and audio file per side. A fact belongs to one deck. Card: one direction of quizzing derived from a fact. The forward card (front → back) always exists; the reverse card (back → front) is optional and needs a non-empty back. Groups are one per deck (exclusive categories); tags are many per deck (cross-cutting labels).
Content format Front and back are Markdown, hard-wrapped (one newline in the source is one line break on the card), with Stella’s own inline syntax on top. Raw HTML is never passed through. All of these can be mixed within a side:
Syntax Renders as Notes **bold**, *italic*, # heading, - item, 1. item, [text](url) Normal Markdown {#RRGGBB}text{/} Colored text The hex must be exactly 6 digits {base|reading} Ruby/furigana, e.g. {漢字|かんじ} No braces, pipes or newlines inside; doesn’t nest {tts:en}text{/tts}, {tts:ja}text{/tts} A read-aloud button plus the text (browser speech synthesis, no audio file needed) Only en and ja; the closing tag is {/tts}, not {/} {center}...{/center} A centered block Sides are justified by default. A color, tts or furigana span can’t straddle the boundary: nest it inside $formula$ Inline math (KaTeX) No $ or newline inside $$formula$$ Display math (KaTeX) May span lines For example:
{center}What is the Pythagorean theorem?{/center}{center}$$a^2 + b^2 = c^2$$ For a right triangle with legs $a$, $b$ and hypotenuse $c$.{/center}{center}This combines **everything**: {#22aa55}color{/}, {tts:en}speech{/tts}, and {漢字|かんじ} furigana.{/center}Plain-text clients, like the e-ink sync device, get all of this stripped to bare text: furigana becomes base（reading）, and every other construct is unwrapped to its inner content.
Media Each side can carry one image (jpg, png, gif, webp) and one audio file (mp3, ogg, wav, m4a, webm, aac, flac). With cards.autoplayAudio on, audio plays as soon as its side is shown.
summary:
Data model

  • Group: an optional folder for decks. A deck belongs to at most one group.
  • Deck: a named collection of facts (name up to 32 characters, description, optional cover image, optional group).
  • Tag: a free label; a deck can carry any number of them, independent of groups.
  • Fact: the content itself, a front and a back, plus an optional image and audio file per side. A fact belongs to one deck.
  • Card: one direction of quizzing derived from a fact. The forward card (front → back) always exists; the reverse card (back → front) is optional and needs a non-empty back.

Groups are one per deck (exclusive categories); tags are many per deck (cross-cutting labels).
title: Cards

content:
Stella schedules cards with a Go port of Mnemosyne’s SM2 algorithm. After each card you grade how well you remembered it, from 0 (blackout) to 5 (perfect recall), and the grade sets when you see the card next: well-remembered cards come back at ever longer intervals, forgotten ones come back soon.
Settings The review section of the config tunes the scheduler:
Setting Default What it does dayStartsAt 3 Hour (0-23) at which a new study day begins, so a late-night session still counts for the day before nonMemorisedCardsInHand 10 How many not-yet-retained cards are juggled at once maxScheduledIntervalDays 0 Cap on the scheduled interval in days; 0 means no cap randomiseScheduledCards false Shuffle due cards instead of ordering them by interval randomiseNewCards false Shuffle the order in which unseen cards are introduced Day boundaries use the top-level timezone setting (an IANA name such as Europe/Madrid), or the host’s local timezone when it is empty.
summary: Stella schedules cards with a Go port of Mnemosyne’s SM2 algorithm. After each card you grade how well you remembered it, from 0 (blackout) to 5 (perfect recall), and the grade sets when you see the card next: well-remembered cards come back at ever longer intervals, forgotten ones come back soon.
title: Reviewing

content:
Decks and groups can be exported and imported as archives. An export carries the content, the media, and each card’s scheduling state and review history, so an imported deck resumes where it left off.
Exporting Export a deck or a group from its page. The endpoints are:
GET /decks/{id}/export: a deck zip GET /groups/{id}/export: a group zip Importing Import from the decks page, by uploading a file or pasting one from the clipboard. Stella accepts:
a deck zip, with deck.json at the root and the media it references under media/ a group zip, with group.json at the root and one deck folder per deck under decks/, each laid out like a deck zip a bare deck JSON file, in the same shape as deck.json Archives are limited by server.bodyLimit (10 MiB by default, see Configuration).
Writing a deck by hand A hand-written deck.json only needs the content. Facts without scheduling data are created as unseen cards, plus a reverse card when reverse is true:
{ "name": "Spanish", "description": "Everyday words", "facts": [ { "front": "la manzana", "back": "apple", "reverse": true }, { "front": "{tts:ja}こんにちは{/tts}", "back": "hello" } ] }See Cards for what front and back can contain.
summary: Decks and groups can be exported and imported as archives. An export carries the content, the media, and each card’s scheduling state and review history, so an imported deck resumes where it left off.
title: Import & export

content:
Stella can expose a Model Context Protocol server, so an AI assistant can create decks and cards for you, tag and group them, and edit or move existing cards.
mcp: enabled: trueThe endpoint is <your Stella URL>/mcp (StreamableHTTP transport), on the same port as the web UI.
Authentication In single-user mode /mcp has no auth at all: keep it on a trusted network.
In multi-user mode it accepts two kinds of credential:
A bearer token from /settings/tokens. Put it in the MCP client’s config as Authorization: Bearer <token>. OAuth. Stella acts as its own OAuth Authorization Server for MCP clients (dynamic client registration, PKCE, a consent screen), on top of the OIDC login. Point an OAuth-capable client (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Claude.ai custom connectors, …) at <publicURL>/mcp and it discovers the flow by itself. Connected apps can be revoked from /settings/tokens. Refresh tokens stay valid for mcp.refreshTokenDays days (30 by default), after which the client goes through the consent screen again. For example, with Claude Code:
claude mcp add --transport http stella https://stella.example.com/mcpTools Area Tools Decks create_deck, list_decks, rename_deck, delete_deck, set_deck_group, set_deck_reverse Groups create_group, list_groups, rename_group, delete_group Tags create_tag, list_tags, rename_tag, delete_tag, tag_deck, untag_deck Cards create_card, create_cards, edit_card, move_card, delete_card, list_recent_cards, get_card_image Media fields on create_card and edit_card take http(s) URLs only; Stella downloads the files into its own media store.
Agent skill The repo ships agent skills under skills/:
stella-cards — the main skill: the card format and every tool in detail, so an agent can write well-formatted cards without trial and error. stella-japanese-decks — conventions for Japanese decks (colour code, furigana, {tts:ja}, card archetypes). stella-vocabulary-decks — conventions for Spanish vocabulary decks. Install them into your agent (for Claude Code, copy the folders into ~/.claude/skills/).
summary: Stella can expose a Model Context Protocol server, so an AI assistant can create decks and cards for you, tag and group them, and edit or move existing cards.
title: MCP server

content:
stella-x4 is a standalone spaced-repetition firmware for the Xteink X4 e-ink reader. It runs the same SM2 review loop offline, from the SD card, and syncs with a Stella server over WiFi.
Connecting a device Create a token in /settings/tokens. Give the device your Stella URL and that token (see the stella-x4 README for how). The device then syncs in explicit sessions. Each session uploads the reviews done on the device, downloads any decks that changed on the server, and exchanges scheduling state in both directions (the most recent change wins).
What syncs Server decks show up on the device as read-only mirrors. Editing, deleting, and choosing which decks to study happen on the server. Reviews done on the device land in the server’s review history, and are safe to upload more than once. Cards reach the device as plain text: the card formatting is stripped, furigana becomes base（reading）. The sync API lives under /api/x4 and only accepts bearer tokens.
summary: stella-x4 is a standalone spaced-repetition firmware for the Xteink X4 e-ink reader. It runs the same SM2 review loop offline, from the SD card, and syncs with a Stella server over WiFi.
title: Device sync

content:
Stella A self-hosted spaced-repetition web app. The scheduling engine is a faithful port of Mnemosyne’s SM2 algorithm, rewritten in Go and wrapped in a small HTMX + Tailwind web UI.
These pages are published at stella-docs.contre.io from the docs/ folder of the stella repository. Start with Self hosted to get it running, then Configuration.
Users & login: single-user or multi-user with OIDC. Cards: the card content format. Reviewing: how the review queue works. Import & export: moving decks and groups between instances. MCP server: letting an AI assistant manage your decks. Device sync: studying offline on an e-ink device.
summary:
Stella

A self-hosted spaced-repetition web app. The scheduling engine is a faithful port of Mnemosyne’s SM2 algorithm, rewritten in Go and wrapped in a small HTMX + Tailwind web UI.
